newsitem.title: CHINA: China offers $120,000 reward for Tibet bomber.
newsitem.headline: China offers $120,000 reward for Tibet bomber.

text.p: China has offered a reward of one million yuan ($120,000) for information leading to the arrest of those responsible for a bombing in the Tibetan capital, Lhasa, last week that damaged part of the city centre, officials said on Monday.

The notice of the reward was issued in the Lhasa Evening News shortly after a bomb exploded in the early hours of December 25 outside a government office, shattering windows for a radius of 100 metres (yards), a government official said by telephone.

No arrests had yet been made following the blast, which officials described as the largest bombing to be set off so far, apparently by anti-Chinese activists, in Tibet, said the official who declined to be identified.
"No one has yet been arrested and we are now mobilising and deploying our forces," he said.

China regularly blames followers of Tibet's exiled Buddhist god-king, the Dalai Lama, for anti-Chinese unrest that erupts sporadically in the strategic mountainous region that straddles the Himalayas and runs along China's sensitive border with India.
